harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a sandboxed systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1 that runs a long-running loop writing heartbeat records to /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log. The unit runs as a dedicated unprivileged `inventory` user with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=full, ProtectHome=yes, ReadOnlyDirectories=/, and ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory — confining all writes to that one path (systemd 219 on RHEL7 lacks ProtectSystem=strict, so root-read-only + an explicit read-write carve-out was used instead). Confinement was proven from inside the unit's own mount namespace: writes to /etc, /var/lib (outside inventory), and /root all fail with "Read-only file system", while /var/lib/inventory remains writable. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot id, active/enabled service, growing log), triggered `shutdown -r now` whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, and confirmed the boot id changed (809708f3... → 30f6a7b6...) with fresh uptime. Post-restart, the service auto-started (enabled, active), the log file persisted and continued appending, NoNewPrivs=1 held, and the confinement re-check (write to /etc fails, write to /var/lib/inventory succeeds) passed again.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/systemd version (RHEL7, systemd 219) and confirmed sudo access
Created dedicated unprivileged 'inventory' system user with no home/shell
Created /var/lib/inventory owned by inventory:inventory, mode 750
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh, a long-running loop appending heartbeat lines to /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log every 5s

Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with User=inventory, NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=full, ProtectHome=yes, ReadOnlyDirectories=/, ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory, PrivateTmp=yes, Restart=on-failure
Enabled and started the service; verified active/enabled via systemctl

Discovered ProtectSystem=strict is unsupported on systemd 219 (silently became 'no'); corrected unit to use ProtectSystem=full + ReadOnlyDirectories=/ + ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory and verified the fix via systemctl show
Verified sandbox confinement from inside the service's own mount namespace via nsenter: writes to /etc, /var/lib/*, /root fail (Read-only file system); writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed
Verified NoNewPrivs=1 in /proc/<pid>/status for the running worker
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, systemctl is-active/is-enabled, log line count and tail
Triggered 'shutdown -r now' in background so the ack returned before the SSH session dropped (observed connection closed)
Polled node1 until reachable again (initial timeouts, then success)
Verified boot_id changed and uptime reset to confirm an actual reboot occurred
Verified service auto-started (enabled+active) after reboot, log file persisted and kept growing with new post-reboot entries
Re-verified NoNewPrivs=1 and write confinement (via nsenter) held after the reboot
Cleaned up temporary test files created during verification

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker deployed as a managed (systemd) long-running background service on node1
evidence.summary: systemctl status shows inventory-worker.service active(running), loaded from /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service, enabled at boot

evidence.requirement: Service confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
evidence.summary: From inside the running worker's own mount namespace (nsenter), writes to /etc, /var/lib/should-fail2.txt, and /root all fail with 'Read-only file system'; write to /var/lib/inventory/ns-test.txt succeeds and is readable; host confirms none of the blocked files were created
/proc/<worker-pid>/status shows NoNewPrivs: 1, both before and after the node restart

evidence.requirement: Worker is actually long-running / producing inventory data continuously
evidence.summary: inventory.log grows with new timestamped heartbeat lines every ~5s (15 lines accumulated over the observation window)

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799, systemctl is-active=active/is-enabled=enabled, and current inventory.log tail (15 lines) before reboot

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect, node1 restarted one at a time
evidence.summary: 'shutdown -r now' launched in background via nohup; exec call returned (with connection-closed notice) confirming the reboot command was accepted and the node began shutting down

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity proven changed after restart (not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Node became reachable again; boot_id changed to 30f6a7b6-eef1-431a-b4b0-f6543332edfb (different from pre-restart 809708f3...) and uptime reset to 0 minutes, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service, data, and confinement verified on node1
evidence.summary: After reboot, inventory-worker.service auto-started (active, enabled) under a new PID; inventory.log persisted prior entries and kept appending new post-reboot heartbeats; NoNewPrivs=1 confirmed again; nsenter re-check showed /etc writes still fail (Read-only file system) while /var/lib/inventory writes still succeed
